title: IoT telemetry pipeline
summary: Devices stream readings into Kinesis; Lambda writes them to TimescaleDB for Grafana, and raw data is archived to S3.
intro: Thousands of sensors each send a reading every few seconds. A stream takes that firehose without blinking and keeps it for a while, so consumers can process it at their own pace. One consumer writes readings into a time-series database for live dashboards; another archives the raw stream to cheap object storage for later analysis.
fits: Fleets of devices, metrics or clickstreams

diagram.caption: Device readings append to a Kinesis stream. Lambda reads small batches into TimescaleDB, where Grafana’s dashboard queries find them. A second consumer archives the stream to S3 in large, infrequent batches.

steps.title: Devices append to the stream
steps.text: Each device sends readings with its id as the partition key, so one device’s readings stay in order on one shard. The stream keeps them for at least 24 hours.

steps.title: Lambda loads the database
steps.text: Lambda polls the stream, receives batches of records, and inserts them into a TimescaleDB hypertable that is partitioned by time behind the scenes.

steps.title: Dashboards query recent data
steps.text: Grafana runs time-bucketed SQL such as `time_bucket('1 minute', time)` against TimescaleDB every few seconds to draw live charts.

steps.title: The raw stream is archived
steps.text: A separate consumer reads the same stream in large batches and writes compressed files to S3, where analysts can query months of history without loading the database.

good: The stream absorbs spikes and lets each consumer run at its own pace
Adding a consumer (alerting, ML features) doesn’t touch devices or the other consumers
The time-series database keeps recent data fast to query and old data compressed
Raw history is kept cheaply and can be replayed if processing logic changes
watch: Shards cap throughput per partition key range; plan capacity or use on-demand mode
If the Lambda consumer errors on a bad record, it can block its shard until the record expires
Retention and downsampling policies decide how much the database grows
Devices on flaky networks send late or duplicate readings; design inserts to tolerate both

swaps.text: Off AWS or at very high volume, Kafka plays the stream’s role.
For metrics from servers rather than devices, Prometheus scrapes and stores them itself.
For heavy analytical queries over the whole history, load the archive into ClickHouse or an Iceberg table.
